sanskrit: ihed asātha na paro gamātha- -imaṃ gāvaḥ prajayā vardhayātha | śubhaṃ yatīr usriyāḥ somavarcaso viśve devāḥ krann iha vo manāṃsi ||
english: Remain here; go not away — O cattle, multiply this one with offspring. Going beautifully, the ruddy cows radiant with soma-lustre: may all the gods fix your hearts here.

sanskrit: imaṃ gāvaḥ prajayā saṃ viśadhvam ayaṃ devānāṃ na mināti bhāgam | asmai vaḥ pūṣā marutaś ca sarve asmai vo dhātā savitā suvāti ||
english: O cattle, enter this one together with your offspring; he does not diminish the share of the gods. Pūṣan and all the Maruts drive you for his sake; Dhātṛ and Savitṛ urge you on for him.

sanskrit: anṛkṣarā ṛjavaḥ santu panthāno yebhiḥ sakhāyo yanti no vareyam | saṃ bhagena sam aryamṇā saṃ dhātā sṛjatu varcasā naḥ ||
english: May the paths be thornless and straight by which our friends go to seek the bride for us. May Bhaga, may Aryaman, may Dhātṛ unite and send us forth with lustre.

sanskrit: yena mahānagnyā jaghanam aśvinā yena vā sūrā | yenākṣā abhyaṣicyanta tenemāṃ varcasāvatam ||
english: With that by which the Aśvins anointed the hip of the great naked one, or with that of Sūrā — with that by which the dice were anointed — with that endow her with lustre.

sanskrit: yad varco akṣeṣu sūrāyāṃ ca yad āhitam | yad goṣv aśvinā varcas tenemāṃ varcasāvatam ||
english: Whatever lustre is laid in the dice, and whatever is placed in the Sūrā drink, whatever lustre is in cattle — O Aśvins, with that endow her with lustre.

sanskrit: yo anidhmo dīdāyāpsv antar yaṃ viprāsa īḍate adhvareṣu | apān napān madhumatīr apo dā yābhir indro vāvṛdhe vīryāvān ||
english: He who shines without fuel in the midst of the waters, whom the inspired priests praise at sacrifices — O Son of Waters, grant the honey-sweet waters by which Indra, the mighty, grew strong.

sanskrit: idam ahaṃ ruśantaṃ grābhaṃ tānūdūṣim apa nudāmi | yaḥ śico bhadro rocānas tam ud acāmi ||
english: This dazzling, body-blemishing seizer — I push it away. That which shines bright and auspicious in the flames — I raise that up.

sanskrit: asyai harantu stapanaṃ brāhmaṇā avīraghnīr ud acantv āpaḥ | aryamṇo agniṃ pary etu kṣipraṃ pratīkṣante śvaśuro devaraś ca ||
english: May the brāhmaṇas bring hither the headdress for her; may the waters — not slayers of heroes — rise up. May she quickly go around Aryaman's fire; the father-in-law and brother-in-law await her.

sanskrit: śaṃ te hiraṇyaṃ śam u santv āpaḥ śaṃ methir bhavatu śaṃ yugasya tardma | śaṃ ta āpaḥ śatapavitrā bhavantu śaṃ patyā tanvaṃ saṃ spṛśasva ||
english: Auspicious to you be the gold, and auspicious be the waters; auspicious be the union, auspicious the piercing of the yoke-pin. Auspicious to you be the waters purified a hundredfold; touch your body together with your husband in well-being.

sanskrit: yathā sindhur nadīnāṃ sāmrājyaṃ suṣuve vṛṣā | evā tvaṃ samrājñy edhi patyur astaṃ paretya ||
english: Just as the bull has engendered the Sindhu's sovereignty over the rivers — so be you a sovereign queen, going home to your husband's house.

sanskrit: samrājñy edhi śvaśureṣu samrājñy uta śvaśruvām | nanānduḥ samrājñy edhi samrājñy uta devṛṣu ||
english: Be a sovereign queen among the fathers-in-law; be a sovereign queen over the mothers-in-law as well. Be a sovereign queen over the sisters-in-law; be a sovereign queen over the brothers-in-law too.

sanskrit: yā akṛntann avayan yāś ca tatnire yā devīr antām̐ abhito 'dadanta | tās tvā jarase saṃ vyayantv āyuṣmatīdaṃ pari dhatsva vāsaḥ ||
english: Those divine women who cut and wove, those who on both sides fixed the borders — may they clothe you to old age; put on this garment full of life.

sanskrit: jīvaṃ rudanti vi nayanty adhvaraṃ dīrghām anu prasitiṃ dīdhiyur naraḥ | vāmaṃ pitṛbhyo ya idaṃ samīrire mayaḥ patibhyo janaye pariṣvaje ||
english: They weep for a living man yet lead the ritual forth; the men have pondered the long procession onward. What boon they have stirred up here for the ancestors — that comfort be for husbands, an embrace for the bride.

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ syonaṃ prajāyai te dhārayāmy aśmānaṃ devyāḥ pṛthivyā upasthe | tam ā rohānumādyā suvīrā dīrghaṃ ta āyuḥ savitā kṛṇotu ||
english: A firm, gentle stone I hold for you for offspring, in the lap of divine Earth. Mount it, you who are praised and blessed with good heroes; may Savitṛ make your life long.

sanskrit: devas te savitā hastaṃ gṛhṇātu somo rājā suprajasaṃ kṛṇotu | agniḥ subhagāṃ jātavedāḥ patyā patnīṃ jaradaṣṭiṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: May the god Savitṛ take your hand; may king Soma make you rich in offspring. May Agni Jātavedas make the fortunate wife, together with her husband, live to old age.

sanskrit: gṛhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā jaradaṣṭir yathāsaḥ | bhago aryamā savitā purandhir mahyaṃ tvādur gārhapatyāya devāḥ ||
english: I take your hand for good fortune, so that you may grow old with me as your husband. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, Purandhi — the gods have given you to me for household mastery.

sanskrit: yenāgnir asyā bhūmyā hastaṃ jagrāha dakṣiṇam | tena gṛhṇāmi te hastaṃ mā vyathiṣṭhā mayā saha ||
english: With that by which Agni took the right hand of this Earth — with that I take your hand; do not falter together with me.

sanskrit: dhātā te hastam agrahīt savitā hastam agrahīt | bhagas te hastam agrahīd aryamā hastam agrahīt | patnī tvam asi dharmaṇā- -ahaṃ gṛhapatis tava ||
english: Dhātṛ took your hand; Savitṛ took your hand. Bhaga took your hand; Aryaman took your hand. By sacred law you are wife — I am your householder.

sanskrit: mameyam astu poṣyā mahyaṃ tvādād bṛhaspatiḥ | mayā patyā prajāvatī saṃ jīva śaradaḥ śatam ||
english: May she be mine, my nurturer — Bṛhaspati has given you to me. Live together with me as husband, bearing offspring, for a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā vāso vy adadhāc chubhe kaṃ bṛhaspateḥ praśiṣā kavīnām | tenemāṃ nārīṃ savitā bhagaś ca sūryām iva pari dhattāṃ prajāyai ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned a garment for beauty, by the instruction of Bṛhaspati among the wise. With that, may Savitṛ and Bhaga clothe this woman for offspring, even as they clothed Sūryā.

sanskrit: gṛhās tvā prorṇuvantu varcasā bhagena jyotiṣmad idaṃ prati muñcasva vapuḥ | uṣā iva sūryasya saṃdṛśi ||
english: May the houses enfold you with lustre and good fortune; let go of this luminous form — as Dawn in the sight of the sun.

sanskrit: indrāgnī dyāvāpṛthivī ha pūṣā mitrāvaruṇā bhago aśvinobhā | bṛhaspatir maruto brahma soma imāṃ nārīṃ prajayā vardhayantu ||
english: Indra and Agni, Heaven and Earth, and Pūṣan, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bhaga, both Aśvins, Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Brahman, and Soma — may they all increase this woman with offspring.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir prathamaḥ sūryāyāḥ śīrṣe keṣām̐ akalpayat | tenemām aśvinā nārīṃ patyā saṃ śobhayāmasi ||
english: Bṛhaspati first arranged Sūryā's hair upon her head. With that we adorn this woman together with her husband, O Aśvins.

sanskrit: idaṃ tad rūpaṃ yad avasta yoṣā jāyāṃ jijñāse manasā carantīm | tām anv artiṣye sakhibhir navagvaiḥ ka imaṃ vidvān vi cacarta pāśam ||
english: This is that form which the woman put on below — you wish to know the wife moving with her mind. I shall pursue her together with the Navagva companions; who, knowing this, has untied this snare?

sanskrit: ahaṃ vi ṣyāmi mayi rūpam asyā vedad it paśyan manasaḥ kulāyam | na steyam admi manasod amucye svayaṃ śrathnāno varuṇasya pāśam ||
english: I shall loose her form into myself — he who sees knows the nest of the mind. I do not consume a stolen thing; freed by the mind, loosening Varuṇa's noose of my own accord.

sanskrit: imaṃ vi ṣyāmi varuṇasya pāśaṃ yena tvābadhnāt savitā suśevaḥ | uruṃ lokaṃ sugam atra panthāṃ kṛṇomi tubhyaṃ sahapatnyai vadhu ||
english: This Varuṇa's noose I loosen, with which Savitṛ the benevolent bound you. A wide world, an easy path — this I make for you, O bride, together with your husband.

sanskrit: ud yacchadhvam apa rakṣo hanātha- -imāṃ nārīṃ sukṛte dadhāta | dhātā vipaścit patim asyai viveda bhago rājā pura etu prajānan ||
english: Rise up; smite away the demon; place this woman in good fortune. Dhātṛ the wise has found the husband for her; may king Bhaga go before, knowing the way.

sanskrit: bhagas tatakṣa caturaḥ pado bhagas tatakṣa catvāry uṣpalāni | tvaṣṭā pipeśa madhyato vardhrān sā no astu sumaṅgalī ||
english: Bhaga has fashioned the four feet; Bhaga has fashioned the four lotuses. Tvaṣṭṛ has carved the leather thongs in the middle — may she be auspicious to us.

sanskrit: enājyena haviṣā prajāyai ca vareṇyam | paśubhyaś cakṣuṣe ca kaṃ sam agniṃ sam idhīmahi ||
english: With this clarified butter as oblation — for offspring and the excellent, for cattle and for sight — let us kindle Agni fully together.

sanskrit: sukiṃśukaṃ vahatuṃ viśvarūpaṃ hiraṇyavarṇaṃ suvṛtaṃ sucakram | ā roha sūrye amṛtasya lokaṃ syonaṃ patibhyo vahatuṃ kṛṇu tvam ||
english: The bridal conveyance is fair with kiṃśuka flowers, all-formed, golden-hued, well-rolling, well-wheeled. Mount it, O Sūryā, into the world of immortality; make the bridal journey gentle for husbands.

sanskrit: mā hiṃsiṣṭāṃ kumāryaṃ sthūne devakṛte pathi | śālāyā devyā dvāraṃ syonaṃ kṛṇmo vadhūpatham ||
english: Let not the post harm the girl on the god-made path. We make the divine gate of the house, and the bride's path, gentle.

sanskrit: brahmāparaṃ yujyatāṃ brahma pūrvaṃ brahmāntato madhyato brahma sarvataḥ | anāvyādhāṃ devapurāṃ prapadya śivā syonā patiloke vi rāja ||
english: Let brahman be yoked behind, brahman in front; brahman at the end, brahman in the middle, brahman on all sides. Reaching the god-city unassailed, benign and gentle, reign in the world of your husband.
